fieldValues.title: Every claim shows what in the research base backs it or contradicts it
fieldValues.move: Each claim in a text carries a visible evidence line built from links to claims, problems and quotes in the research base: backed, contradicted, or unlinked. Outside material, such as a news article being answered or a conversation transcript, is brought in as a source whose passages become quotable records the writer can cite. The writer sees the gaps and decides what to do about them; agents propose links, the writer accepts them.
fieldValues.does_not_fix: Keeping abandoned framings as attempts to review later (SP-56), and whether the evidence base itself is sound. How a stance chooses to attack or support a claim, which is the stance remedy.
fieldValues.falsifier: A writer asked, for any claim in a finished piece, what backs it and what contradicts it cannot answer from the evidence line without searching the research base by hand, or a source brought in cannot have a passage quoted from it.
fieldValues.return_when: When one real piece, answering a news article, has been written with evidence lines and the owner has said whether every claim could be checked.
